subject: Early-adopter latency waiver & credit — Novapulse
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@novapulse.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.example.com
Cc: procure@novapulse.ai
Date: Tue, 28 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Early-adopter ask — latency target / credits

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the discussion yesterday. Novapulse is excited to move forward as an early-adopter for Redwood’s dedicated offering for our recommendation API. Two asks from procurement and product leadership to keep the kickoff on the proposed timeline: 

1) A temporary latency waiver for the first 90 days: our production traffic is bursty during business hours (median p95 target 220ms). We’re asking for a one-90-day latency SLO carveout that allows p95 up to 350ms without service-credit penalties while we complete integration.

2) An early-adopter commercial credit to offset onboarding risk — a one-time usage credit equal to two weeks of estimated tokens (they suggested an initial $12k offset).

We understand this is non-standard. If you can route to your deal desk and flag for executive approval (we need contract countersign by 11/07 to meet our fiscal quarter internal deadlines), that would be a huge help. I’ve attached a draft SOW for context.

Thanks,
Aisha Khan
Head of Platform Partnerships
Novapulse

Attachments: Novapulse_SOW_draft.pdf
From: ben_carter@redwood.example.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.example.com
Date: Tue, 28 Oct 2025 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Early-adopter ask — latency target / credits

Marissa / Lauren,

Looping you in — Novapulse wants a 90-day temporary p95 latency carveout (allow up to 350ms p95) and a one-time early-adopter credit (~$12k). They need contract countersign by 11/07.

Quick notes:
- This is a small pilot (expected steady state ~18M tokens/month) but heavy peak bursts during ET daytime hours.
- They’ll go Dedicated; isolation constraints mean we can’t rely on cross-tenant burst capacity.
- I’m proposing a conditional carveout instead of a permanent SLA change: 90 days, explicit telemetry + weekly check-ins, and automatic reversion to standard SLOs.

Attachments: latency_analysis_q3.xlsx (short-run cost + risk model)

Can we get deal-desk and finance eyes? If exec signoff is required, tagging Lauren for final concurrence. If acceptable, I’ll update the SOW language and deliver a condensed Remediation/No-penalty schedule for legal.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter | Account Exec, Strategic Deals | Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.example.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com, jonas_weber@redwood.example.com
Date: Wed, 29 Oct 2025 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Early-adopter ask — latency target / credits

Ben —

Reviewed quickly with Finance and Legal. High-level position: we can support a time-boxed operational carveout but need clear guardrails to limit risk and precedent. Proposed terms: 

- 90-day carveout window starting on prod cutover date. During window, p95 up to 350ms will not trigger service-credit deductions.
- Customer accepts a monitoring plan with weekly telemetry snapshots to our Ops channel; Redwood may terminate carveout early if we detect sustained degradations (defined as >3 consecutive days where 24h rolling p95 exceeds 400ms).
- Early-adopter credit capped at $12,000 and payable as a usage credit applied against the first billing cycle after cutover.
- Require a signed amendment that explicitly states this is a one-time, non-precedential concession; clause auto-expires.

Financial impact: Jonas ran the risk model — worst-case incremental cost if we absorb peak load is roughly $9k over the 90 days (based on latency_analysis_q3.xlsx). With the $12k credit, we’re within acceptable variance, but we should tie the credit to an onboarding milestones checklist (3 items) so we can pause credits if milestones aren’t met.

If Lauren approves commercial and exec-level concurrence, Legal will draft the amendment language and Procurement can proceed to countersign.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole | Head of Deal Desk | Redwood Inference
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.example.com
Date: Sun, 2 Nov 2025 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Early-adopter ask — latency target / credits

Team —

I’ve reviewed Marissa’s summary and Jonas’s cost notes. I approve the following, with conditions listed below: 

Approval (executive concurrence):
- 90-day time-boxed latency carveout (p95 up to 350ms) starting on customer production cutover.
- One-time early-adopter usage credit up to $12,000.

Conditions:
1) Credit is milestone-gated: 50% on successful production cutover (health checks green for first 48 hours), remaining 50% after completion of the first weekly ops review and onboarding checklist completion.
2) Amendment language must include a non-precedent clause and explicit auto-expiry after 90 days.
3) Redwood reserves right to terminate carveout early if sustained degradations occur (Marissa’s definition is acceptable).
4) Ben to close the SOW update and coordinate countersign by 11/07; if countersign slips beyond that date, approval is void and must be re-requested.

Marissa — please instruct Legal to draft the amendment and attach the milestone checklist. Jonas — please confirm the worst-case cost model in the doc and include a short note for Finance sign-off. Ben — communicate the approved terms to Novapulse and get them to confirm the cutover target.

Good work getting this across the line.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop | VP Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
